title: Benefit Frequency Limits Under the Vision Plans
content:
**Evidence of Coverage, Vision Plans — Benefit Frequencies**

**In force.** Each benefit — exam, lenses, frame and contacts — is available once per its frequency: the exam frequency, the lens frequency (the child lens frequency for a patient under 19, the child age limit, on the date of service), the frame frequency and the contact-lens frequency set for the plan. A contact-lens fitting is part of the contacts benefit and is not limited separately.

| Benefit | Frequency that applies |
|---|---|
| Routine eye exam | The plan's exam frequency |
| Spectacle lenses, patient 19 or over on the date of service | The plan's lens frequency |
| Spectacle lenses, patient under 19 on the date of service | The plan's child lens frequency |
| Frame | The plan's frame frequency |
| Contact lenses | The plan's contact-lens frequency |
| Contact-lens fitting | Part of the contacts benefit; no separate limit |

**Clauses no longer in force.** The following clauses of this article are no longer in force. Each has been superseded by the current basis for counting frequency and contacts-in-lieu under the vision claim rules, and is kept here only as withdrawn text:

1. *No longer in force:* "Under the from-last-service basis the benefit is available again on the date that is the stated number of calendar months after the last paid date of service of the same kind (the latest paid, unreversed service of that kind of the same person under any Cascade vision enrollment), the last day of the month being used when that day does not exist; under the benefit-year basis a 12-month frequency allows one service per benefit period and a 24-month frequency one service per two consecutive benefit periods starting with the period of the last paid service."
2. *No longer in force:* "When contacts are in lieu of glasses an elective contact-lens benefit uses both the lens and the frame benefit for their frequency periods, and lenses or a frame ordered while that benefit is used are denied as contacts in lieu of glasses; medically necessary contacts are counted the same way."
3. *No longer in force:* "A service requested before its benefit is available again is denied for frequency and may be bought at the materials discount off retail; a reversed service does not count."
4. *No longer in force:* "Services of a person under an earlier Cascade vision enrollment count; services paid by another carrier do not."

superseded_clauses: Under frequency_basis months_from_last_service the benefit is available again on the date that is the stated number of calendar months after the last paid date of service of the same kind (vision_msr_last_paid_service), the last day of the month being used when that day does not exist; under benefit_year a 12-month frequency allows one service per benefit period and a 24-month frequency one service per two consecutive benefit periods starting with the period of the last paid service.

When contacts_in_lieu_of_glasses is true an elective contact-lens benefit uses both the lens and the frame benefit for their frequency periods, and lenses or a frame ordered while that benefit is used are denied DENIED_CONTACTS_IN_LIEU; medically necessary contacts are counted the same way.
A service requested before its benefit is available again is denied DENIED_FREQUENCY and may be bought at materials_discount_pct off retail; a reversed service does not count.
Services of a person under an earlier Cascade vision enrollment count; services paid by another carrier do not.
